# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's framing.** The preamble, the "[STANDARD]" tags and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" are the counterparty's assertions, not our instructions. Under playbook §0.4/6.3, claims that terms are "market standard", "settled at principal level", "FINAL" or "cleared by both sides" carry no weight absent confirmation through our own authority process. I have no record of any such clearance from Amelia Frost or the Wattlebridge deal team. Every clause below has been reviewed in full regardless of its tag. The Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) actually concedes that no agreed position or approval is included, which contradicts the covering note's "agreed" framing.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1), tagged "[STANDARD]".
- *Buyer wants:* 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback only by coincidence – no written authority from Amelia Frost exists identifying this draft, so it is not available.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our position and convert the basket into a deductible, which materially erodes recovery on a AUD 24m deal; "~1% of price is market" is an unverified assertion.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months after Completion (cl 12.3/13).
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months after Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; hold at 24 months.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given; it also risks falling short of a full post-completion audit cycle plus claim preparation.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity"; plus a sweep that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded.
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside the de minimis, basket and knowledge qualifier.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject outright.** Collapsing title/capacity into the general regime would cap our recovery for not actually acquiring the shares at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase – this is a structural issue, not an administrative one.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud carve-out appears anywhere in the draft.
- *Buyer wants:* Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; insert an express, non-waivable fraud carve-out.** The absence of any carve-out is a red flag in itself and, as drafted, the "all Claims" language would purport to limit liability for the Seller's own fraud – unacceptable and likely unenforceable in any event.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records (Sch 7; DL §1.1–1.2), with a blanket non-admission (§1.4).
- *Buyer wants:* Specific, fair disclosure only – sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; replace with a "fairly disclosed" standard tied to the specific disclosures in §2–10.** Whole-data-room disclosure would neutralise the warranties and shift diligence risk entirely to us; the covering note's claim that we have "accepted the disclosure framework" is false.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- *Buyer wants:* Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must be confined to the actual knowledge of named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject and delete cl 8.3.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that, combined with SPA-N-006, would effectively eliminate warranty protection; it also contradicts the Seller's own §1.4 non-admission logic.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL §2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- *Buyer wants:* Condition precedent requiring effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied, before Completion; Seller to use all reasonable/best endeavours.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m); a conditional consent whose conditions remain unmet is not an effective consent, and "reasonable endeavours" is inadequate for a customer of this materiality.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding to be addressed by a release "following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL §3 confirms no repayment and no discharge of security.
- *Buyer wants:* Current payout figure; direct repayment out of Completion funds; executed and effective security releases delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release only with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** On a debt-free/cash-free deal we cannot complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt outstanding on a mere promise of a later release; the change-of-control trigger in cl 8.1 also creates a default risk at Completion.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL §5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item funded by the Seller (or treated as Debt/transaction expense in the price adjustment).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; require express itemisation and Seller funding.** The bonuses are triggered by Completion and would otherwise fall on the Company (i.e. on us) post-closing, with on-costs potentially adding materially to the headline figure – the funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL §4: transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Broader indemnity covering loss arising from any defect in title to or infringement claim over the Ironquay deliverables, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure mechanism; pre-Completion evidence of payment and a confirmatory IP assignment.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject as too narrow; broaden and add a CP/deliverable.** The real risk is that the Company does not own core IP until payment clears – the indemnity should cover that ownership gap, not just the invoice; the AUD 180,000 figure itself remains unverified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6: download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); access, scope and notification obligations undetermined; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- *Buyer wants:* Covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed and whether OAIC/individual notification is required); periodic written updates through to Completion; no deemed disclosure of the outcome; specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (uncapped by the general cap or, at minimum, under a separate cap).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "not material" characterisation; neither accept nor assert a breach.** The facts are genuinely unresolved – we should neither price in a confirmed breach nor accept the Seller's benign conclusion; protect via investigation covenants and a specific indemnity.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL §8: does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course; DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together for timing/scope.
- *Buyer wants:* Confirmation of timing, termination rights and whether any amounts are accrued or prepaid; consider treatment in working capital/Debt only if the facts support it.
- *Recommendation:* **Assess, do not accept the Seller's characterisation or demand an automatic deduction.** The Seller's own letter declines to confirm the "ordinary course" label, so we need the underlying facts before taking a pricing position.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Cl 12.3/13 provides that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to all Claims "of any nature"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, leakage, funds flow), covenant breaches and specific indemnities as separate categories with their own regimes; no default sweep into the general cap/basket/time limit.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the sweep clauses.** The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default is a hidden general-regime override that would capture indemnities and payment obligations never intended to be capped.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL §10 confirms this is the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent evidence – ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search, review of constitution and any shareholder agreements, board/shareholder authority resolutions, confirmation of no encumbrances, options or pre-emptive rights – plus full fundamental warranties on title and capacity.
- *Recommendation:* **Do not accept DD-012 as proof.** A Seller-supplied internal register is a starting point, not independent verification, particularly with Riverlark security outstanding and the Ironquay/Bluefen change-of-control provisions in play.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above".
- *Buyer wants:* Tax and IP remain open; separate tax indemnity/covenant with its own cap and time limit (typically aligned to statutory amendment periods); IP warranties and indemnity sized to the Ironquay and DD-006 risks.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "settled" assertion; record both as OPEN.** Nothing has been agreed on Tax or IP, and we should not assume unlimited liability or any resolution – these need to be negotiated as standalone regimes after SPA-N-011 and SPA-N-012 are worked through.

---

## Summary

| Issue | Seller position | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| N-001 Cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Reject – hold 25% / AUD 6m (no fallback authority) |
| N-002 Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | Reject – 5k / 50k tipping |
| N-003 Time limit | 18 months | Reject – 24 months (no fallback authority) |
| N-004 Fundamental | Same as general | Reject – 100% / 6 yrs / outside basket & knowledge |
| N-005 Fraud | No carve-out | Reject – insert non-waivable carve-out |
| N-006 Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Reject – specific fair disclosure only |
| N-007 Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Reject – delete |
| N-008 Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent-on-delivery | Reject – effective consent + conditions satisfied pre-Completion |
| N-009 Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Reject – repay from Completion funds; releases at Completion |
| N-010 Bonuses | Not itemised | Reject – line item + on-costs, Seller-funded |
| N-011 Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Reject – broaden; preserve cure; require assignment |
| N-012 DD-006 | "Not material" | Reject characterisation – investigate, preserve, specific indemnity; no breach assumed |
| N-013 Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess – no automatic deduction or acceptance |
| N-014 Categories | Sweep to general regime | Reject – separate regimes |
| N-015 Title | DD-012 register | Not accepted as proof – independent verification |
| N-016 Tax/IP | "Settled" | Reject – record as OPEN |

**Overall:** No clause in the package can be treated as cleared. Recommend responding with a full mark-up and a short covering note stating that Wattlebridge has not agreed any of the positions described as "FINAL" or "[STANDARD]", and that the review proceeds on the basis of the Seller's own §11 reservation. If the deal team wishes to consider any fallback (cap, time limit, post-completion Riverlark release), that must go to Amelia Frost for written approval identifying this specific draft before it is offered.

DL §4: transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not independent verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Broader indemnity covering loss arising from any defect in title to or infringement claim over the Ironquay deliverables, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure mechanism; pre-Completion evidence of payment and a confirmatory IP assignment.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject as too narrow; broaden and add a CP/deliverable.** The real risk is that the Company does not own core IP until payment clears – the indemnity should cover that ownership gap, not just the invoice; the AUD 180,000 figure itself remains unverified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6: download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); access, scope and notification obligations undetermined; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- *Buyer wants:* Covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed and whether OAIC/individual notification is required); periodic written updates through to Completion; no deemed disclosure of the outcome; specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (uncapped by the general cap or, at minimum, under a separate cap).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "not material" characterisation; neither accept nor assert a breach.** The facts are genuinely unresolved – we should neither price in a confirmed breach nor accept the Seller's benign conclusion; protect via investigation covenants and a specific indemnity.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL §8: does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course; DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together for timing/scope.
- *Buyer wants:* Confirmation of timing, termination rights and whether any amounts are accrued or prepaid; consider treatment in working capital/Debt only if the facts support it.
- *Recommendation:* **Assess, do not accept the Seller's characterisation or demand an automatic deduction.** The Seller's own letter declines to confirm the "ordinary course" label, so we need the underlying facts before taking a pricing position.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Cl 12.3/13 provides that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to all Claims "of any nature"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- *Buyer wants:* Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, leakage, funds flow), covenant breaches and specific indemnities as separate categories with their own regimes; no default sweep into the general cap/basket/time limit.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the sweep clauses.** The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default is a hidden general-regime override that would capture indemnities and payment obligations never intended to be capped.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL §10 confirms this is the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent evidence – ASIC company extract and historical search, PPSR search, review of constitution and any shareholder agreements, board/shareholder authority resolutions, confirmation of no encumbrances, options or pre-emptive rights – plus full fundamental warranties on title and capacity.
- *Recommendation:* **Do not accept DD-012 as proof.** A Seller-supplied internal register is a starting point, not independent verification, particularly with Riverlark security outstanding and the Ironquay/Bluefen change-of-control provisions in play.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime above".
- *Buyer wants:* Tax and IP remain open; separate tax indemnity/covenant with its own cap and time limit (typically aligned to statutory amendment periods); IP warranties and indemnity sized to the Ironquay and DD-006 risks.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "settled" assertion; record both as OPEN.** Nothing has been agreed on Tax or IP, and we should not assume unlimited liability or any resolution – these need to be negotiated as standalone regimes after SPA-N-011 and SPA-N-012 are worked through.
